title: Maintenance Ledger — Containment Line C
body:
HILFER — PLANT MAINTENANCE
Extract through 25 OCT 98
Equipment group: SEC-TEST / containment line
Prepared for: Engineering weekly review
Maint. contact: Tito
15 SEP — POS-REL-01
Relay sticking at changeover. Contacts pitted. Replaced relay and checked travel with line isolated. Normal on three cycles.
Disposition: Closed.
30 SEP — POS-REL-01
Same position is sticking again. See Tito's note in the September 30 mail chain. No spare assembly on the shelf. Ordered one; monitor at each changeover.
Disposition: Open / parts.
08 OCT — POS-REL-01
Replacement fitted. No hang observed under load. Return to service.
Disposition: Closed. Previous repair remains in history.
09 OCT — SEN-03
Periodic comparison against SEN-01/02 outside tolerance. Cleaned connection and repeated check. Return reading within test band.
Disposition: Closed after check.
18 OCT — SEN-03
Drift on morning comparison. Adjustment held for the afternoon run.
Disposition: Closed.
25 OCT — SEN-03
Third call this month. Reading low against the other channels during the check. Adjusted again. Tito requested instrument bench time; no slot was available before Monday.
Disposition: Closed after recalibration; bench review pending scheduling.
Other open items
SEN-04 — calibration interval shortened pending a permanent sensor replacement.
SHD-TEMP-01 — temporary shielding fitted under approved exception; replacement not yet received.
Tito's note, 25 OCT:
I can keep checking SEN-03, but if it moves again we ought to take it out and put it on the bench. The last two adjustments didn't last very long.
Ledger status reflects work orders, not a complete evaluation of instrument reliability.

title: Interim Operating Restrictions — Rev. C
body:
ENGINEERING / SYSTEMS RELIABILITY
23 October 1998
Interim operating note — test area and adjacent access
Prepared by Tim
Distribution: Operations, Instrumentation, Site Safety
Use this revision for the remaining pre-demonstration runs. Rev. B may be retained for history but is not to be used for shift planning.
1. Sensor comparison
For ordinary trend checks, use the paired SEN-01 and SEN-02 readings as the working reference. A disagreement from SEN-03 must still be logged. Do not average it away or record it as a failed sensor without an instrument check.
2. Occupancy
Use the shorter entry periods on the posted route sheet. Engineering has not approved an increase in time in SEC-TEST. If a task runs over, stop and reassign the remaining work to the next eligible person. Operations should not treat an unfilled shift as an automatic extension for the worker already inside.
3. Rotations
No one is to be assigned on the assumption that the previous shift's estimated dose was zero. HR/Operations need the cumulative figures before they put names against a route.
4. Temporary hardware
SHD-TEMP-01 remains an exception. Check its fastening and position at the start of each run. Replacement is still the preferred disposition.
These measures have brought the last set of monitored runs within the revised operating limits. That is why I am recommending continued restricted work, not unrestricted access.
If the instrument comparison changes over the weekend, call Engineering before making a schedule out of this one.
Tim
Systems Reliability

title: Instrument Exception — 26 October
body:
INSTRUMENTATION EXCEPTION REVIEW
Entered: 26 OCT 98 / 17:12
Reference: SEC-TEST, pre-demonstration run
Logged by: Instrumentation Desk
Observed at 16:50:
SEN-01 — elevated indication
SEN-02 — elevated indication
SEN-03 — no corresponding increase
Both elevated channels returned toward the earlier range within the next several minutes. The automatic event marker was retained.
Checks completed:
- Channel recording sequence reviewed for obvious time offset.
- No confirmed loss of SEN-01 or SEN-02 power during the interval.
- SEN-03 calibration history shows field adjustments on 09, 18 and 25 October (see maintenance ledger).
- No bench comparison of SEN-03 was available at the time of this review.
Disposition: UNVERIFIED ANOMALY
The signals do not agree. We have not established whether the elevated indication represents the actual area condition or an instrument problem. Do not delete the three traces.
For the demonstration go/no-go decision, Engineering has been asked to review the event with the current operating restrictions. An instrument exception does not, by itself, authorize or cancel the test.

title: Occupational Health — Cases for Follow-up
body:
OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH
28 October 1998 / 16:10
Prepared by José Carlos
Distribution: Medical; restricted review for Legal and HR
Six employees have been referred for follow-up where a possible connection to facility work cannot yet be excluded. This is a follow-up list. It is not a list of six confirmed occupational exposure injuries.
Case notes for classification:
• Jessica, EMP-JESSICA — reported nausea, headache, fatigue and skin irritation after leaving Sector C on 13 October. OH-008 did not clear her for the 12–18 October work period. A new restricted-duty authorization was issued 21 October for SEC-ADJ; this did not alter the earlier finding. Reassess after the 27 October event.
• One worker reported symptoms beginning 16 October, eleven days before the Incident. Present complaint needs review, but onset is outside the official Incident interval.
• Another nearby-area worker reported symptoms on 22 October; work history and other causes still being checked.
• Three additional employee reviews were opened or updated after 27 October. The available information is not equally complete for all three.
Two cases currently meet the reporting criteria for serious exposure associated with the defined Incident window. The remaining cases should stay on the follow-up list pending additional history and results. Their exclusion from that reporting category is not a finding that the complaints have no occupational basis.
Please don't use the count of six as the number of confirmed cases. Conversely, the reportable count should not be used to close these follow-ups.
José Carlos

title: Recovery Operations — Initial Closeout
body:
OPERATIONS / ENGINEERING
Emergency action closeout
27 OCT 98 — 22:05
Incident INC-19981027
OP-R01 | 15:30–17:15
Purpose: stabilize the affected containment subsystem before further deterioration.
Result: immediate containment condition stabilized following manual intervention. Restricted access remains in effect.
OP-R02 | 19:15–21:30
Purpose: retrieve the isolated diagnostic modules needed to establish the failure sequence and confirm current containment behavior.
Result: critical telemetry recovered and accepted for analysis.
These actions addressed the immediate stabilization and diagnostic requirements identified in the emergency meeting. They were not routine work and required controlled entries.
Outstanding:
- Equipment remains in the affected area.
- Full cleanup and return-to-service have not been authorized.
- Additional retrieval or entry is not covered by this closeout.
- Staffing and exposure estimates must be reviewed before any proposed additional work.
Operations sign-off: initial response tasks complete.
Engineering sign-off: necessary diagnostic material received.
Site Safety: access restrictions remain in force.

COMMUNICATIONS / DRAFT — NOT RELEASED
Last saved: 02 NOV 98, 02:14
Editor: Guy
For internal revision only
The 29 October version says 'containment event.' Engineering is now describing a failure of the containment assembly. We need to say what failed, or say we still don't know. 'Event' by itself doesn't tell anyone anything.
Medical:
Six people being followed. Two in the serious Incident category. Which names are we leaving out when we print only the second number? The dates and criteria need to be beside the count.
Jessica — symptoms on the 13th; different authorization on the 21st; exposed during the breach. Don't collapse those into a single 'medical leave' entry.
Tito — roster says eligible before the third entry. The camera shows an injury. 'Available for duty' was not checked afterward. Someone needs to call Medical before we use that field.
Recovery:
First entry contained the immediate problem.
Second entry brought out the missing readings.
Third entry was for the prototype.
That third line is not in the approved summary. It should be.

On 27 October the demonstration resulted in a failure of part of the containment system. Emergency personnel subsequently stabilized the affected area and retrieved diagnostic equipment. A later recovery entry was authorized for the program prototype. During that entry a technician was seriously injured. The final medical outcome—

title: External Correspondence — Compliance Routing
body:
HILFER / COMMUNICATIONS COMPLIANCE
Procedure CC-4 — revision 15 SEP 98
Applies to: classified program and Incident-related external correspondence
Messages prepared on the internal workstation may be submitted to the external mail gateway. The workstation's acceptance notice confirms receipt for routing; it does not certify external delivery.
Before release, the gateway checks:
- destination authorization
- attachment classification and origin
- current approved excerpt list for the program
- whether an outgoing statement is still under departmental review
Restricted documents are not to be forwarded as original attachments. Where an approved excerpt exists, the routing copy may use that excerpt instead. Unapproved material remains in the internal record. A release copy and its routing disposition are retained in the correspondence log.
Employees who need an unqualified technical or medical statement released must obtain the appropriate departmental clearance. The help desk cannot override that clearance.
Questions about a returned or held message should refer to the routing number, not the local draft filename.
Communications Compliance

Recorder: DVR-04-L
Camera input: CAM-04

Parent segment: SEG-R03-01
Review extract reference: SEG-R03-01:review
The local acquisition event log and parent segment directory identify a recording interval of 28 OCT 98, 06:43:00–06:43:27. The extraction register associates the recovered picture blocks with this parent segment and camera input. The playable review extract contains 14.375 seconds, not the entire 27-second indexed interval. No missing pictures were reconstructed, repeated or stretched.
Picture overlay observed during the read test: TCR 10-09 18:37:11. This text stays unchanged while the recovered pictures and recorder sequence positions advance. It cannot be used as an advancing event clock. The acquisition event log is separate from that picture overlay; the overlay does not establish the capture date. The cause of the stale text was not established by this check, and no corrected picture timestamp is asserted.
The extraction register preserves the association between this review extract and SEG-R03-01. It does not assign an absolute event time to each recovered frame or establish that every indexed second survived.
This is a local recorder and extraction check, not independent confirmation of which operation used the corridor. Operational movement and custody records must be compared separately before an operational association is filed.
No personal identity, medical outcome or cargo contents are certified here.

The readable extract is 14.375 seconds; the carrier indexes the larger 06:43:00–06:43:27 parent interval. This check does not claim a complete 27-second picture sequence.
Separately, Operations checked its own corridor movement log. That contemporaneous entry records equipment transport for OP-R03 through SEC-R03-ACCESS at 06:43 on 28 OCT 98, after the 06:34 resumption. The collection entry associates the corridor recorder's SEG-R03-01 carrier with that route and operation. This operational timing comes from the movement log, not the text burned into the picture and not a transcription of Systems Integrity's report.
Together these checks corroborate the recovered extract's custody and operational association. They do not repair the displayed TCR 10-09 18:37:11, date individual recovered frames, or explain why that text is stale.
No worker identity is established from the image or this custody check. The movement entry does not certify an injury, a final medical status, the cargo contents or completed delivery. Those are separate questions requiring their own sources.
